text: On 12 October 2012, Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) applied to the Budapest police department for authorisation to hold a demonstration on the road leading to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) stated that the demonstration would be held on the hard shoulder of the road leading to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport, which was not ordinarily used for traffic.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: One of the declared objectives of the demonstration was to draw the public's attention to the precarious financial situation in which the employees of Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport would find themselves if salary cuts envisaged by the company managing the airport were carried out.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The demonstration was scheduled to be held between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m. on 17 October 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) specified that it was expected that about fifty to 100 persons would participate in the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) specified that it was intended that an open letter would be read out at the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 14 October 2012, the Budapest police department registered the application to hold a demonstration on the road leading to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 14 October 2012, the Budapest police department informed Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) that it was necessary to schedule a meeting with the organisers in order to clarify details regarding the programme of the demonstration and the number of police officers that would be required to secure the event.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) and the Vice-President of the United Civil Aviation Trade Union met with the representatives of the Monor police department on 14 October 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The representative of the Monor police department suggested that the demonstration be held at another location, since the planned venue on the road leading to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport would endanger traffic.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) assured the police that the demonstrators would respect traffic rules.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) assured the police that the demonstrators would only occupy the part of the road not used for traffic.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) assured the police that the demonstrators would distribute flyers to car passengers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) assured the police that the organisers would call off or halt the demonstration if it was not in compliance with the relevant legal provisions.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 14 October 2012, the Monor police department forbade the demonstration planned for 17 October 2012 on the road leading to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Monor police department was of the view that the planned demonstration would endanger traffic.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Monor police department was of the view that the planned demonstration would render Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport inaccessible, infringing passengers' right to leave the country.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Monor police department was of the view that the demonstration would breach the traffic code, since those parts of the road not used for traffic were not supposed to be accessed by pedestrians or be used for parking.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 17 October 2012, the United Civil Aviation Trade Union (the first applicant) and Mr A. Csorba (the second applicant) requested judicial review of the Monor police department's decision forbidding the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants relied on their right to freedom of expression in requesting judicial review of the Monor police department's decision forbidding the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants relied on their right to freedom of assembly in requesting judicial review of the Monor police department's decision forbidding the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants argued that a demonstration could only be forbidden on the grounds of a need to ensure traffic safety if there were no alternative means of access to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants argued that the demonstration would not constitute any greater hindrance to traffic than would roadworks.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: By a decision of 19 October 2012, the Budapest Surroundings High Court (Budapest Környéki Törvényszék) dismissed the applicants' complaint requesting judicial review of the Monor police department's decision forbidding the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Budapest Surroundings High Court (Budapest Környéki Törvényszék) endorsed in essence the Monor police department's reasoning for forbidding the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Section 8(1) of Act no. III of 1989 on the Right to Assembly provides that if the holding of an event subject to prior notification seriously endangers the proper functioning of the representative bodies or courts, or results in a disproportionate hindrance of the circulation of traffic, the police may ban the holding of the event at the place or time indicated in the notification, within 48 hours from the receipt of the notification by the authority.
